detail.text: Backfilled record of the build session of 2026-10-07. Entries T-0002 onward were written at the end of the session from the session's own transcript, not at the time each event happened. Timestamps on these entries are the time of writing.

Started from an uploaded scaffold (docs, schemas, two small Python files, no engine). Built the governance core around it: phase engine, hash-chained ledger, reference vault, comparator, metrics, CLI. Commit 15cfc91 (v0.1).

Could not reach github.com/openai/math from the build sandbox (HTTP 403 from the sandbox proxy). The reference corpus named in the docs is therefore unconfirmed. One web search suggested OpenAI published ten results with Lean proofs in 2026; that was not verified and no source was read in full.
Wrote the reference answer for fixture F-0002 as 6732 from mental arithmetic. Brute force gives 6834. Caught in the same step by a brute-force check, before any test used it.

v0.1 scored a transfer test from a single run on the unseen problem. A solver that would have solved it anyway was scored TRANSFERRED. Shipped in 15cfc91 with the gap listed in CLAUDE.md; a v0.1 test asserted the flawed behaviour.

v0.1 defaulted the answer vault to a directory inside the repository for all problems, so references sat next to the code a solving agent works in. Shipped in 15cfc91 with the gap listed in CLAUDE.md.

Wilson's second instruction was 'I have the adjustments of exactly what it's supposed to be' with no file attached. Interpreted it as: implement the four weaknesses named in the previous reply (control arm, blindness, ablation, problem pool). This reading was stated to Wilson and not confirmed by him before the work was done.

v0.2: transfer is scored from a treatment/control pair on one unseen problem; real problems are refused unless the vault is outside the repository; attempts must record model, knowledge cutoff, web access and code execution; stages can be skipped per run; calibration bank added. Corrects T-0005 and T-0006.

First version of the preflight self-test ran its fixture loop with FMA_VAULT still set, so it would have written fixture references into the real answer vault. Caught because the calibration/preflight unit test failed; fixed before any real vault existed by unsetting FMA_VAULT inside the self-test.

The self-test expected TRANSFERRED where the control arm answered a different integer. The engine left that comparison UNRESOLVED (non-identical text), so the pair was INCONCLUSIVE. The engine was right and the test expectation was wrong.

T-0010 exposed a design gap: with only the textual comparator, every wrong integer answer would need manual adjudication. Added an 'integer' adapter that calls two bare integers equal or a MISMATCH and declines anything else.

The first calibration set used all 30 problems in Batch 1 and left no unseen same-family problems for transfer tests; the engine would have refused every transfer run. Caught on review before the plan was committed. Added a 20-problem holdout (seed 20261008).
'fma status' reported the next action as 'question' for a run whose condition skips every pre-solve stage. Committed in 400412e, found by a manual flow check, fixed in b3d2a4d with a test.

First sync of v0.2 to the Mac delivered commit 400412e, not the final b3d2a4d: the staged tarball was a stale copy. The first 'READY' preflight on the Mac was therefore run against 400412e. Caught by reading the git log on the Mac; re-sent under a fresh file name, verified HEAD b3d2a4d, and re-ran preflight.

Blindness of the build session: the calibration answers (50 files) were generated inside the build session's sandbox and copied to the Mac by it. The session did not print or read them, but it had access. It also printed five calibration problem statements to check their wording. One of them (39^72 mod 13) has the obvious answer 0, so some bank problems are trivial.

Verification scope: the unit tests were run only in the cloud sandbox (Python 3.13). On the Mac only the preflight self-test was run, inside a Linux sandbox with Python 3.10 that has no pytest. Nothing has been run under native macOS Python.

Leftovers on the Mac in ~/projects that the build session could not delete: frontier-math-apparatus-v0.1.tar.gz, frontier-math-apparatus-v0.2.tar.gz and fma-vault.tar.gz. The last contains the calibration answers.

Chose the vault location ~/projects/.fma-vault (a sibling of the repository) without asking Wilson, so that preflight could pass. It satisfies the engine's outside-the-repo rule and is still readable by any process on the machine.

Saved the Pilot 0 plan to the research lab as 07-next/frontier-math-apparatus-pilot-0.md in blackswanlabz-research-lab (branch verifier-green), plus one llms.txt line. Chose the main lab folder out of four similarly named ones without asking. Left uncommitted. The lab's offline verifier reported OK; its shell wrapper printed 'set: Illegal option -o pipefail' under sh first.
The lab page says the build was 'checked in Linux sandboxes with Python 3.10 and 3.13'. That is imprecise: the unit tests ran on 3.13 only, and 3.10 saw only the preflight self-test (see T-0016).

Wilson's standing rule, given 2026-10-07: this is a research program and everything is recorded, including failures and mistakes. Added this program log, the rule in CLAUDE.md and README design rule 11, and a preflight check on the log chain.

Not done and not claimed: no problem has been solved with the apparatus, no metric has been computed on real runs, AIL/MoIE/FCVE are not implemented in it, and the solver model for Pilot 0 has not been chosen.

Corrected the macOS wording on the lab page (07-next/frontier-math-apparatus-pilot-0.md) to match T-0016, and added a 'Build record: mistakes and failures' section there summarising this log. Lab verifier still OK offline. This entry was appended on the Mac after commit 1e73360 and is uncommitted, as are the lab changes.
